markdown_report:
Select an **independently referenced, mutation-calibrated temporal diagnostic** before changing NextItNet training. At 10% progress, reliable fault detection is a feasible foundation; current evidence does not establish a temporal modeling failure.

Three starting insights guide this choice. Uniform fitted-target HR@10 reaches 0.9362–0.9953, but competitive candidates reduce it; these training results cannot establish generalization. Movies_and_TV loses 0.2652 with prefix-lexical competitors, motivating precise-discrimination checks without inferring incompatibility or satisfied needs. Deployment parity and internal category identity remain unavailable, limiting otherwise healthy in-memory results.

Three literature insights refine the approach. NextItNet implies causal and numerical convolution constraints, but full receptive-field coverage cannot identify dilation schedules [1]. Shuffling studies and conditional permutation methods caution that sensitivity depends on plausible replacement distributions [2,3]. Mutation research identifies unstable or inactive operators, motivating controls, severity sweeps and held-out mutation evaluation [5–7].

The framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Implementation integrity | Independent convolution/block references | Detection beyond designed mutations |
| Temporal dependence | Distance-resolved matched swaps | Useful versus implausible sensitivity |
| Candidate discrimination | Frozen competitive candidates | Transfer to pinned validation |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Critical assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Mutation-calibrated probes [1,5–7] | 4/6/6 | Originality: useful integration, established principles. Potential: actionable debugging, limited accuracy relevance. Difficulty: no retraining, independent oracles and restoration are substantial. |
| Matched local history swaps [2,3] | 6/7/6 | Originality: controlled adaptation, established matching. Potential: resolves distance effects, residual mismatch persists. Difficulty: existing scorer, sparse matching support. |
| Fixed uniform/frequency negative mixture [4] | 2/6/3 | Originality: direct application, previously proposed. Potential: targets observed competition, false negatives threaten validation. Difficulty: small sampler change, careful pool handling. |

For the selected idea, test readout, padding and dilation mutants against specifications frozen from the corrected baseline. Compare pre-normalization convolutions with explicit indexed sums; compare residual, skip and summed block outputs using the actual normalization/activation order. Include impulses, multichannel random inputs, boundaries and left padding. Reachability alone cannot detect numerically wrong dilation.

Run unchanged repeats, clone/reload and identity-injection controls. Calibrate numerical thresholds on separate training inputs, then freeze them before held-out sites/operator variants. Report mutation activation, local effect, propagation and detector response separately; surviving mutants need not be equivalent. Sweep identity, subtle and destructive severities. Treat weak reachable-field sensitivity as learned behavior, not a defect.

Preserve the diagnostic/interpreter interfaces, ModelView compatibility, final-nonpadding readout and one deployed NextItNet checkpoint/category. Bound loader snapshots to four batches and 32 rows/batch; restore parameters, attributes, hooks, modes and RNG even after exceptions. Keep all four routes, seeds and training limits fixed. Reload parity remains unavailable without host access. Only pinned macro validation HR@10 selects accuracy improvements; these diagnostics neither train nor deploy mutants.

idea.description: Calibrate the existing NextItNet structural and distance-resolved probes against isolated inference defects using an independent numerical architecture reference, negative controls, severity sweeps and held-out mutation sites/operator variants. Reuse each category's single fitted checkpoint and bounded training inputs. Mutants are temporary executions of its parameters, never independently fitted predictors, deployment candidates or fused scores.
idea.motivation: The supplied measurements establish competitive-candidate sensitivity but do not establish defective temporal reasoning. Low sampled-pair error and modest positive embedding cosine do not demonstrate deployment correctness. The previous proposal also overestimated the diagnostic power of receptive-field coverage: different dilation schedules can cover the same history while computing different values. Independent numerical references and controlled mutation evaluation can expose such faults while distinguishing detector failure, inactive perturbations and weak learned sensitivity. This is a debugging investment, not an established HR@10 improvement; the negative-sampling intervention remains a more direct subsequent accuracy experiment.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve existing measured diagnostics and explicit unavailable statuses. Use view.model as the actual trained module, retaining item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility. Require no unavailable reviews, ratings, item categories, prices, stores or simulator traits.

Snapshot at most four batches and 32 rows/batch from the family-specific loader, whose rows are (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Freeze disjoint calibration and evaluation row manifests before examining results, recording deterministic batch/row indices and content hashes. These are training diagnostic inputs, not validation holdouts; unidentified users may overlap across partitions. Record sequence lengths, occupied positions, finite exclusions and supported comparisons. Final readout is the largest nonzero index; exclude all-padding rows. Loader rows lack stable user identities, so do not report user-bootstrap intervals or independent-user uncertainty.

Freeze an independent architecture specification from the host-supplied corrected baseline before applying mutations: residual-block variant, convolution order, kernel sizes, expected dilations, explicit padding/cropping, normalization axes and epsilon, affine parameters, activation order, skip projections and padding-mask locations. Reference configuration must never come from potentially mutated layer attributes. Weights and affine tensors may be cloned from the fitted model. If the authoritative architecture specification is unavailable, report the reference-dependent checks as unavailable; do not reconstruct a supposedly independent oracle solely from the mutated instance. A shared specification error remains a limitation.

Implement each reference convolution by explicit indexed sums: y[b,t,o] = bias[o] + sum over c,j of W[o,c,j] * x[b,t-p_left+j*d,c], with out-of-range inputs zero and causal p_left=(k-1)*d, p_right=0. Match the actual Conv1d/Conv2d layout and any groups; reject unsupported layouts explicitly. Compare outputs before normalization. Use deterministic synthetic impulses at early, interior and final positions, multiple channels, and distinct nonzero tap weights in disposable primitive tests, plus multichannel nonconstant random inputs. Primitive synthetic weights test operator semantics and are neither trained nor saved recommendation weights. Separately compare actual fitted weights against the reference, where learned inactivity can hide defects. Full receptive-field coverage is insufficient to identify the dilation schedule.

For whole blocks, independently reproduce the exact normalization and activation order. Compare residual branch F(x), skip branch S(x), and F(x)+S(x) separately. Compute channel-wise normalization explicitly, including epsilon and affine parameters; perturb other times and batch members to detect incorrect normalization axes. Disable dropout and choose nonconstant multichannel inputs to reduce erased signals. Apply only masks required by the frozen specification, including specified masks after biased operations. Padding invariance must not be assumed where the clean architecture does not guarantee it. Preserve the existing future-invariance, aligned-prefix, ModelView scoring, distance-resolved ablation, shuffle and embedding probes and their interpretive limits.

Predeclare operators, sites, severities and diagnostic tolerances before evaluation. Include count-minus-one readout, future-exposing centered/asymmetric padding, and a single-convolution dilation change with correctly adjusted causal padding. Readout mutants require short left-padded rows where the erroneous index differs. Padding and dilation mutations must preserve output shape; account for F.pad wrappers, convolution attributes, cropping and cached padding metadata. Future perturbations test causality; numerical layer references detect causal but wrong dilation. A reachable perturbation with no learned effect is not itself a defect.

Use an explicit operator configuration table. Identity severity leaves every value unchanged. For dilation, use d+1 as a subtle mutation and 2*d+1 as a larger mutation, always adjusting left padding; for padding, shift one unit of padding from left to right and then use centered padding, retaining total padding. Record exact resulting values because severity is operator-specific rather than comparable across families. Count-minus-one is a discrete readout defect with an identity control, not a fabricated continuous severity. Predeclare a seeded site ordering across early, middle and late blocks and both conv1/conv2 positions. Retain inactive sites and difficult survivors rather than selecting detectable cases. Additional normalization-axis and misplaced-mask mutants may be reserved as held-out families when the baseline specification supports them.

Run unchanged-model repeats, an ephemeral state clone/reload control, and zero-severity injections through the identical wrapper and scoring pipeline. A temporary clone is an execution control of the same fitted parameters, never an independently trained or deployed model. Pin evaluation mode, preprocessing, device and precision. Measure clean numerical variation on calibration rows; predeclare threshold construction, such as atol=max(1e-5, 10*maximum clean absolute discrepancy) with rtol=1e-4 for float32, and record the calibration discrepancy and resulting thresholds. Evaluate pass/fail elementwise using abs(actual-reference) <= atol + rtol*abs(reference). Large clean discrepancies require investigation, not automatic tolerance inflation. Freeze thresholds before evaluation; report raw absolute/relative errors alongside decisions. Exact top-10 disagreement is a separate, tie-sensitive outcome, not a substitute for numerical comparison.

Keep predetermined evaluation rows and mutation sites unseen during threshold calibration. Where feasible, reserve whole operator families as well; explicitly label the distinction between held-out sites and held-out families. If a family was used to design its own detector, report that dependence and do not claim broad fault-detection generalization. Record site selection seed, operator implementation version, frozen specification hash, row manifests, precision, device/library versions and actual mutated values in trial-local artifacts.

For each mutation, record whether the requested value changed, execution-hook counts, local activation discrepancy, logit discrepancy, ranking disagreement and fault-specific detector outcome. Distinguish attempted injection, exercised site, local effect, propagation and detection. Report all attempted cases and justified exclusions with operator/site/severity denominators. Structural mismatch and behavioral detection are separate outputs. A surviving mutant is demonstrated equivalent only where equivalence has actually been established; otherwise label observed inactivity or unresolved survival. Present detection-versus-severity curves and observed clean alarm rates rather than one pooled kill rate. Without an independently verified clean implementation, call alarms observed clean violations, not established false positives. Any target-ranking degradation measured here is fitted-training diagnostic degradation, never validation accuracy loss.

Ensure each temporary wrapper registers the actual model as a child module and routes feature/scoring calls to that same instance. Avoid closures capturing a different model or cached clean features. Invoke modules as module(x), since direct .forward(x) bypasses their hooks. Verify the mutation path with hook counters and a controlled perturbation. torch.func.functional_call substitutes parameters/buffers, not dilation, padding or arbitrary Python attributes; use explicit temporary module replacements or exception-safe attribute changes for those operators. Clone supplied tensors because in-place operations can modify substitution dictionaries.

Use an exception-safe context manager. Snapshot cloned parameters and buffers, including nonpersistent buffers; ordinary and cached padding attributes; every module's training flag; existing hook registries; Python/NumPy/custom-generator RNG state; and CPU/CUDA torch RNG through fork_rng for the active device. Remove only newly installed hooks and preserve existing hooks. Restore state in finally. state_dict hashes alone cannot establish restoration because state_dict omits ordinary attributes, hooks, modes, RNG and nonpersistent buffers, and its tensors are shallow references. After both successful probes and a deliberately raised exception, rerun fixed-input clean inference under identical evaluation/RNG conditions and compare outputs, attributes, hooks, buffers and flags. Abort subsequent interpretation if restoration fails. Do not let diagnostics alter training's RNG stream.

Category routing should come from existing host context when available. Never infer identity from catalog size or silently label fallback category index 0 as correct. Preserve unknown identity and unavailable macro aggregation when needed. Generated working/predict.py reload parity remains unavailable without a host execution interface; ephemeral module reload controls do not establish deployment parity. Actual predictor parity, if host-supported, must cover all four routes, mappings, truncation, left padding, short/maximum-length histories, final readout, scores and ordered top-10.

The interpreter must embed measured values, definitions, support, calibration configuration, held-out coverage, exclusions and unavailable interfaces. Distinguish structural violations, learned sensitivity, training memorization, qualitative feedback and independent validation. Aggregate qualitative feedback supplies hypotheses, not item-level incompatibility labels. No evidence here establishes satisfied needs, current intent or unobserved user traits.

No training or predictor architecture change is required. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl; DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts stay trial-local. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch. Execute on one GPU within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Bound primitive inputs, mutation sites and severities in a frozen configuration, and report omitted checks if the diagnostic budget is exhausted. Deploy exactly one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint/category without ensembles, checkpoint averaging or score fusion. Do not read other trials or reuse their checkpoints. Any later inference change must update the embedded predictor writer and probes consistently. Only the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 selects accuracy improvements.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        model = self.view.model
        saved = clone_full_execution_state(model)
        clean_inputs = fixed_clean_inputs()
        try:
            with preserve_all_rng_states(), torch.no_grad():
                model.eval()
                before = clean_inference(model, clean_inputs)
                batches = snapshot_batches(train_loader, max_batches=4, max_rows=32)
                manifest = freeze_calibration_and_evaluation_rows(batches)
                spec = load_authoritative_frozen_baseline_spec()
                metrics, definitions = existing_family_probes(batches)

                if spec is unavailable:
                    record_reference_checks_unavailable()
                else:
                    reference = ExplicitNextItNetReference(spec, clone_tensors(model))
                    # Convolution uses explicit indexed sums; normalization is explicit.
                    # Return pre-normalization convolution, F(x), S(x), and block sum.
                    primitive_inputs = frozen_impulse_boundary_and_random_inputs()
                    primitive_results = compare_operator_semantics(
                        primitive_inputs, distinct_tap_weights=True,
                        multiple_channels=True, reference=reference)

                    controls = run_controls_through_identical_pipeline(
                        model, reference, manifest.calibration,
                        controls=['unchanged_repeat', 'ephemeral_clone_reload',
                                  'identity_injection'])
                    thresholds = freeze_predeclared_threshold_rule(controls)
                    if controls.show_unexplained_large_discrepancy:
                        record_reference_or_clean_failure_and_skip_calibration_claims()
                    else:
                        clean = run_clean_invariants_and_layer_comparisons(
                            model, reference, manifest.evaluation, thresholds,
                            final_readout='largest_nonzero_index')
                        results = []
                        for mutation in frozen_operator_site_severity_manifest():
                            with exception_safe_mutation(model, mutation) as actual_model:
                                wrapper = RegisteredActualModelWrapper(actual_model)
                                verify_execution_path(wrapper, hook_counter=True)
                                result = run_fault_specific_checks(
                                    wrapper, reference, manifest.evaluation,
                                    primitive_inputs, thresholds)
                                results.append(record_injection_local_effect_propagation_detection(
                                    mutation, result, retain_inactive_and_surviving_cases=True))
                            verify_clean_restoration(model, saved, clean_inputs, before)
                        exercise_deliberate_exception_and_verify_restoration(
                            model, saved, clean_inputs, before)
                        metrics.update(operator_site_severity_summaries(
                            clean, controls, results,
                            separate_heldout_sites_and_families=True))

                return {
                    'metrics': merge(metrics, primitive_results_if_available(),
                                     support_exclusions_configuration_and_missingness()),
                    'metric_definitions': merge(definitions, calibration_definitions())
                }
        finally:
            restore_full_execution_state(model, saved, remove_only_new_hooks=True)
            verify_fixed_input_clean_output_and_full_execution_state(model, saved)


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return build_prompt(
        measured_metrics=raw_diagnosis['metrics'],
        definitions=raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        instructions=[
            'Separate structural mismatch, local effect, propagation and detection.',
            'Report calibration thresholds, controls, held-out coverage and support.',
            'Survival does not establish equivalence; sensitivity does not establish accuracy.',
            'Distinguish training diagnostics from pinned validation and user feedback.',
            'Do not infer intent, compatibility or satisfied needs from missing evidence.',
            'Keep deployment parity unavailable unless the generated predictor was checked.'
        ])

originality.positive: Integrates independent numerical NextItNet references, left-padding readout checks, controlled inference mutations and held-out diagnostic evaluation into a family-specific protocol.
originality.negative: Mutation testing, numerical reference implementations and calibration controls are established; the contribution is careful integration rather than a new recommendation algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Could support reliable debugging and later temporal experiments while avoiding additional fitted recommendation models and exposing faults missed by receptive-field coverage.
future_potential.negative: Passing specified mutations cannot establish deployment correctness or useful temporal reasoning, and no evidence connects the proposed diagnostic investment to improved validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses frozen parameters, bounded batches and existing compatibility interfaces without retraining or metadata indexing.
code_difficulty.negative: Independent convolution/block references, mutation-path verification, calibrated held-out evaluation and complete exception-safe restoration require substantially more work than the earlier rating of 3 suggested.

related_work.title: [1] NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Provides the required causal dilated residual convolution family, including residual designs and left padding.
Supports causal invariants and independent layer/block numerical references that account for the actual normalization and activation order.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed mutation-calibration protocol or its detection coverage.
Receptive-field coverage cannot identify a unique dilation schedule, and architectural reachability does not imply a nonzero learned effect.

related_work.title: [2] Does It Look Sequential? An Analysis of Datasets for Evaluation of Sequential Recommendations
contributions: Studies original and shuffled histories across multiple datasets.
Motivates distinguishing order sensitivity from useful sequential information.
limitations: Unrestricted shuffling can alter history plausibility.
Its findings do not establish a temporal failure in the supplied NextItNet checkpoints.

related_work.title: [3] The Conditional Permutation Test for Independence While Controlling for Confounders
contributions: Develops conditional permutation methodology preserving dependence on observed confounders.
Motivates controlled history replacements instead of arbitrary corruption.
limitations: Formal calibration depends on conditional-distribution assumptions.
Matched-history recommendation diagnostics are an adaptation, not an established application demonstrated by this paper.

related_work.title: [4] Supplied training-candidate stress audit and prior research proposal
contributions: Reports weaker fitted-target ranking against frequency-weighted and lexical competitors across all four categories.
Proposes a fixed uniform/frequency training-negative mixture as a minimal subsequent accuracy intervention.
limitations: Training-audit metrics are not pinned validation metrics and may reflect memorization.
Category identity and generated-predictor reload parity remain unavailable; competitors are not verified negatives.
This is supplied experimental context, not an independently published reference.

related_work.title: [5] DeepMutation
contributions: Establishes direct model mutations without retraining.
Supports temporary post-training mutation of frozen networks.
limitations: Output disagreement alone does not establish useful fault detection.
Does not validate the proposed NextItNet operators, references or thresholds.

related_work.title: [6] MuFF
contributions: Identifies instability, poor killability and low sensitivity in existing post-training mutation operators.
Motivates stability controls and separate accounting for local activation changes and downstream effects.
limitations: Its operators do not establish calibrated detection for causal sequential convolution defects.
The proposed severity sweeps and held-out family protocol remain adaptations requiring evaluation.

related_work.title: [7] DeepCrime
contributions: Emphasizes killable but nontrivial mutants and discrimination between weak and strong test suites.
Motivates retaining difficult survivors and avoiding detector evaluation only on faults used during design.
limitations: Its training-distribution statistical framework requires adaptation to a single frozen checkpoint.
Does not justify independent-user inference or training-seed uncertainty estimates from unidentified loader rows.

related_work.title: [8] PyTorch Module and hook documentation
contributions: Documents module registration, invocation, hooks, modes and state handling.
Supports routing wrappers through the actual module and preserving existing hooks during temporary instrumentation.
limitations: Direct forward calls bypass module hooks.
state_dict alone does not capture ordinary attributes, hooks, training flags or all execution state.

related_work.title: [9] PyTorch torch.func.functional_call
contributions: Documents functional substitution of parameters and buffers.
Clarifies why structural dilation and padding changes require additional mechanisms.
limitations: Does not substitute arbitrary Python attributes.
In-place operations can modify supplied substitution tensors, requiring cloned state.

related_work.title: [10] PyTorch convolution implementation
contributions: Exposes convolution padding paths and cached metadata relevant to temporary structural mutations.
Supports checking actual implementation behavior when preserving causal output shape.
limitations: Implementation details are version-dependent; record the installed version.
The implementation under test cannot itself supply an independent correctness oracle.

related_work.title: [11] PyTorch random-number documentation
contributions: Documents torch RNG preservation mechanisms, including fork_rng.
Supports diagnostic isolation from the training random stream.
limitations: Torch RNG preservation does not preserve Python, NumPy or custom-generator states.
RNG restoration alone does not guarantee restoration of model attributes, buffers, hooks or outputs.
